clue.text: Expect garden tool needs power input

indicators.note: needs together with input says the tool requires something put into it
input means something put in, so this letter goes inside the tool

parts.note: a hoe is a garden tool for weeding
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A gardener assumes their tool will need a motor fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' and 'input' together put P, the physics symbol for power, inside HOE.
explanation.definitionFit: To hope for something is to look forward to it as likely, a near synonym of expect.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink drunk before dance

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: high is slang for drunk or intoxicated
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A cocktail knocked back before going off to a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A highball is a long mixed drink of spirits and soda served in a tall glass.

clue.text: Filling food getting father's thanks

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, with the possessive s
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A dad being thanked for a hearty meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is a starchy staple that fills you up, so it is a filling kind of food.

clue.text: Pitiable walkway — mention when returning

parts.note: a path is a walkway

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to cite is to mention

explanation.surface: A sorry-looking footpath brought up again on the way back.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic means arousing pity, so it is a synonym of pitiable.

clue.text: Place to live in settlement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lodging, a place to stay
second meaning: a compromise or arrangement reached between parties

explanation.surface: Somewhere to live in a new settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: Settlement looks like a village, but here it means an agreement, as in reaching an accommodation with rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both housing and a mutually agreed compromise between opposing sides.

clue.text: Loiter in E Sussex resort, second only to Brighton

parts.note: Hove is a seaside town in East Sussex, joined to Brighton

indicators.note: second only to picks just the second letter of the word that follows

parts.note: second letter R

explanation.surface: Hanging about in a south-coast town that ranks behind its famous neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second only to Brighton' sounds like Hove ranking just below Brighton; it is the second letter of Brighton. Brighton and Hove are neighbouring English seaside towns.
explanation.definitionFit: To hover is to linger close by, waiting about, which is what loitering is.

clue.text: Former magistrate new in war-torn Beirut

indicators.note: in places this letter within the others
war-torn means ripped apart, so the letters of the city are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of Beirut, taken as written

explanation.surface: A new figure appearing in the Lebanese capital during conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribune was an official in ancient Rome who protected the plebeians, an old kind of magistrate.

clue.text: Signals for actor's lines to the audience

indicators.note: what reaches an audience is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: queues are lines of waiting people

explanation.surface: Prompts telling an actor when to deliver their lines to the theatre audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'actor's lines' reads as a script, but the 's is 'is'; lines are queues, and 'to the audience' asks for that word as heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Cues are the words or actions that tell an actor when to speak or move, so they are signals.

clue.text: Morning meal — some bananas about right?

indicators.note: about means around, so the bunch goes round the other letter

parts.note: bananas grow and are sold in a bunch

explanation.surface: Is a few bananas about right for a late breakfast?
explanation.definitionFit: Brunch is a late-morning meal combining breakfast and lunch.

clue.text: Audible prank after flatulence affecting the stomach

indicators.note: audible means able to be heard, so the phrase counts by its sound

parts.note: flatulence is gas and a prank is a trick, so gas then trick

explanation.surface: A noisy joke involving wind that upsets someone's insides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places TRICK after GAS, and 'Audible' says the pair is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric is the medical adjective for anything relating to the stomach.

clue.text: Oscar limited by failing faculty of speech

indicators.note: limited by means hemmed in, so this letter sits inside the other word

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Oscar winner held back by losing the ability to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Voice is the power of producing speech, so it is the faculty of speaking.

clue.text: Mind supporter at home

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Someone minding a supporter who is staying in.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain is the organ of thought, often used to stand for the mind.

clue.text: Babble, having knocked back strange spirit

indicators.note: knocked back means sent backwards, so both words are read in reverse

parts.note: rum is old British slang for strange
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: Talking nonsense after downing a peculiar liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum appears twice in different senses, odd and the drink, and 'knocked back' reverses both, though it reads as drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A murmur is a low continuous indistinct sound of voices, close to babble.

clue.text: Refreshment provided by Times press office

indicators.note: provided by means supplied from within the words that follow, so the letters run across them

parts.note: the letters run on across these words

explanation.surface: Drinks supplied by the newspaper's press department.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee, a drink taken as a refreshment.

clue.text: Hideous quality of arranged lessons at home

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The horror of lessons organised for home schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsomeness is the quality of being repulsive, so it is a hideous quality.

clue.text: Startled nearly everyone with a weapon

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: everyone is all
the last letter of the word, dropped
armed means carrying a weapon

explanation.surface: Almost everybody carrying weapons is a frightening thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarmed means suddenly frightened, a close synonym of startled.

clue.text: Avoid breaking peace around centre of armistice

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the anagram wraps the single letter
breaking means shattering, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of peace, taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: middle letter S

explanation.surface: A truce broken around the middle of the ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges PEACE into ECAPE, and 'around' wraps it round S, the centre of armistice.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape something is to avoid it, as in escaping punishment.

clue.text: Thirty-one days inside a yacht harbour

parts.note: March has 31 days, and MAR is its calendar abbreviation
in means inside

explanation.surface: A month spent in the sailing harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' looks like an instruction to put one piece in another, but it simply gives IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a harbour with moorings for yachts and pleasure boats.

clue.text: I had the last of many lines for poem

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: the last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: final letter Y
L is the abbreviation for line, LL for lines

explanation.surface: A poet who had used the last of many lines for a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a short poem describing a peaceful rural scene.

clue.text: Easy to understand cold Shakespearean king

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
King Lear is the title role of a Shakespeare tragedy

explanation.surface: A plain verdict on a chilly Shakespearean monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear means plain and readily understood, as in a clear explanation.

clue.text: Manage over hard period

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read upwards in this down answer

parts.note: to cope is to manage
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Getting through a difficult stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long distinct period of time in history or geology.

clue.text: Island is providing refuge for black bird

indicators.note: providing refuge for means sheltering, so the other letter is held inside

parts.note: I is the map abbreviation for island
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: An island sanctuary sheltering a dark-feathered bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a down-curved bill.

clue.text: Not even make payment to get round politician

indicators.note: to get round means to encircle, so the word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to buy is to pay for something
an MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician

explanation.surface: Paying off a politician to win them over is hardly level dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get round' suggests persuading the politician, but it means surround.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumpy surface is uneven, so bumpy means not even.

clue.text: Wicked devil promises to pay money back

parts.note: an imp is a small devil
IOUs are written promises to repay a debt, standing for I owe you

explanation.surface: A devilish character makes promises to repay what he owes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a reversal signal, but it belongs to the phrase pay money back.
explanation.definitionFit: Impious means lacking reverence for God, close to wicked.

clue.text: Limit on court is party policy

parts.note: a side is one party in a dispute or contest
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A political party's policy is likened to a boundary on a sports court.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideline is the boundary marking the edge of a tennis or basketball court.

clue.text: Go away, taking time off from branch

indicators.note: taking with off from means removing something from the word that follows
off from completes the instruction, saying the letter leaves the branch

parts.note: a shoot is a new branch on a plant

explanation.surface: Clearing out after a break from work at a branch office.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoo is said to drive someone away, so it means go away.
